message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: write

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  run:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - run: echo "Job was automatically triggered by a ${{ github.event_name }} event for branch ${{ github.ref }}"

      - name: Check out repository code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      # - name: Install xmllint and xsltproc
      #  run: |
      #    sudo apt-get update
      #    sudo apt-get install libxml2-utils xsltproc

      - name: Validate structure and lint XSD and XML files
        run: ./.github/scripts/validate-and-lint.sh

      - name: Validate NeTEx XML examples
        run: ./.github/scripts/validate-examples.sh

      - name: Validate negative examples (must-fail)
        run: ./.github/scripts/validate-should-fail.sh

      # Only on push: a pull_request run from a fork gets a read-only token
      # and cannot commit back. Target branches are still normalized by the
      # push-triggered run that follows the merge.
      - name: Commit changes
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        uses: EndBug/add-and-commit@v9 # https://github.com/marketplace/actions/add-commit
        with:
          default_author: github_actions
          message: 'Lint and update documentation tables'
",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs on every push and pull_request with a single job and no concurrency control, so repeated revisions on the same branch or PR can execute in parallel and duplicate work. The P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE pattern (cancel superseded runs; evidence: 4.2.3; Table 4; PDF pp. 7; vm_time_reduction_percent free 1.9, paid 4.1) applies because runs represent the same workflow and branch/PR and a newer revision supersedes older checks. Adding a concurrency group scoped by github.workflow and github.ref isolates branches/PRs (no shared cancellation group) and cancels in-progress older runs when a newer revision starts. This preserves all build and test coverage because the latest run still completes fully, adds no privileged actions, secrets, publishing/deployment operations, or new network access, and does not weaken permissions. The commit-back step is documentation/lint updates, not release or deployment work.",
  "evidence_ids": ["P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE"]
}
